 AFP News Tue, 17 November 2026 at 1:12 pm GMT-8 3 min read NVDA +3.92% 
 ^IXIC -0.74% 
 Jensen Huang resigned as head of Nvidia over revelations of an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, and wider suspicions her firm was funneling Nvidia products into China (I-Hwa Cheng) Concern over the future of the tech sector dragged down stock markets Tuesday, as traders sold off shares linked to the AI industry ahead of an earnings report from crisis-hit chip giant Nvidia. 
 The company was set to announce more bumper revenues and profits in its report, due out after Wall Street closed, but its longer-term growth is shrouded in uncertainty after the United States moved to tighten restrictions on Chinese access to chips. 
 Jensen Huang resigned as head of Nvidia last week over revelations of an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, and wider suspicions her firm was funneling Nvidia products into China. 
 The Nasdaq, the benchmark US tech index, fell a further 0.74 percent Tuesday. 
 "Beyond the usual focus on results, forward guidance, and data center demand, investors will be closely watching the company's first earnings call with Colette Kress as interim CEO following Jensen Huang's abrupt departure," Adam Turnquist at LPL Financial said. 
 "With Huang widely viewed as 'irreplaceable,' attention will center on the leadership transition and the board's timeline for naming a permanent CEO," he added. 
 "Shares have been pressured by the double-edged sword of growing concerns over an AI slowdown and uncertainty surrounding Huang's departure." 
 Huang said Tuesday he was hoping for a comeback, fuelled by support from US President Donald Trump, but that outcome is highly uncertain. 
 Adding to the downbeat mood was news that the US Commerce Department had moved to shut a loophole allowing Chinese companies to access Nvidia's powerful AI chips remotely. 
 The markets were also trying to fathom the consequences of AI firm Anthropic's initial public offering, which is expected in New York on Thursday. 
 The share sale is expected to value the firm, which makes the Claude chatbot, as high as $1.4 trillion, which would make it one of the world's most valuable companies. 
 While Anthropic is widely seen as the leader for AI products, Nvidia has been dubbed the "central bank" of the industry for its investments in startups and providing backstops on loans. 
 By the end of the week, traders are hoping to have more certainty about the commercial future of a technology that has been long on hype but short on profitable products. 
 Traders, meanwhile, sold off some technology-adjacent stock -- Nvidia's price plunged in morning deals before partly recovering. 
 On Wall Street, all three major indexes backed up Monday's steep losses with more negative numbers. The Dow Jones shed 1.64 percent. 
 Story continues Trading in Europe was sluggish all day and tapered dramatically by close, with all three major indexes finishing down. 
 Frankfurt led the way with 2.1 percent losses, and the pattern was similar across Asia.
